_strings.@@552241acf88e: Treaty conformity — CA does NOT conform to federal tax treaties: income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is STILL taxable by CA. Do not carry a federal treaty exclusion onto the state return. (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state's Internal Revenue Code conformity date and its deduction/credit conformity are separate questions; see any law-change lines below.) State note: California does not conform to federal income tax treaties. FTB Pub. 1031 (2025), Section on Tax Treaty, p. 10, verbatim: "A tax treaty between the U.S. Government and a foreign country may exempt some types of income from federal taxation. Generally, unless the treaty specifically excludes the income from taxation by California, the income is taxable." Worked Example 1 (unchanged from the 2024 edition): a resident of China doing research at a California university received $15,000 of teaching/research wages excludable for federal purposes under the U.S.-China treaty — determination: "Although the wages may be exempt from income for federal income tax purposes, the wages will be taxable by California... Tax treaties between the United States and other countries which expressly limit their application to federal income taxes do not apply to California." The $15,000 is included on Schedule CA (540NR), Part II, Section A, line 1a, column C. California also disallows the foreign tax credit and the foreign earned income exclusion (same publication, "Foreign Tax Credit or Foreign Earned Income Exclusion").
